title: Ezekiel 42:15–20
context: Having finished measuring the inner house, the guide leads the prophet out by the east gate and measures the whole area on each of its four sides: east, north, south, and west. Each side measures five hundred, and a wall surrounds the area to separate the holy from the common. In 42:16-19 the measure is given in reeds, while 42:20 gives five hundred cubits; readers differ on how to relate the two figures, and the question stays open. Both traditions read the square enclosure as a picture of the holiness of God’s dwelling, whatever view they take of the temple vision as a whole.

verses.text: Now when he had finished measuring the inner house, he brought me out by the way of the gate which faces toward the east, and measured it all around.
verses.arminianNotes: Now when he had finished measuring the inner house, Arminian readers see the measuring move outward, as the guide brings the prophet out by the gate which faces toward the east.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the east gate is again the point of reference. The prophet will be brought back to this gate in 43:1 to see the glory return.

verses.text: He measured on the east side with the measuring reed five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed all around.
verses.arminianNotes: He measured on the east side with the measuring reed five hundred reeds, Arminian readers see the measuring begin on the east side, the direction associated with the gate and the coming glory.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers observe that the measuring reed was introduced in 40:3. The repeated phrase with the measuring reed stresses that the measuring is careful and complete.

verses.text: He measured on the north side five hundred reeds with the measuring reed all around.
verses.arminianNotes: He measured on the north side Arminian readers find the second side measured with the same figure of five hundred, confirming the regular shape of the enclosure.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the repetition gives the list a rhythm. Each side receives the same measure, together forming the square enclosure that is summarized in 42:20.

verses.text: He measured on the south side five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.
verses.arminianNotes: He measured on the south side Arminian readers observe the third side completed with the same measure, the area taking shape as a perfect square.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers observe that the order of the sides, east, north, south, and west, follows the guide’s movement. The text records the measuring without symbolic comment.

verses.text: He turned about to the west side, and measured five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.
verses.arminianNotes: He turned about to the west side, Arminian readers note that the fourth and last side, again five hundred, completes the circuit that began at the east gate.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the guide turns about, bringing the circuit to a close. The equal sides prepare for the summary of the next verse.

verses.text: He measured it on the four sides. It had a wall around it, the length five hundred cubits, and the width five hundred cubits, to make a separation between that which was holy and that which was common.
verses.arminianNotes: He measured it on the four sides. Arminian readers see the purpose stated plainly: the wall was built to make a separation between that which was holy and that which was common.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that 42:20 gives five hundred cubits, while 42:16-19 speaks of reeds, and readers relate the figures differently. Both traditions read the wall as a sign of God’s holiness.
